title: Economic and social pressure is entering mental-health life through loneliness, housing, digital exposure, and help-seeking stigma
source_unit: St Patrick's Mental Health Services annual Stigma and Attitudes to Mental Health Survey 2026
geography: Ireland; nationally representative adults aged 18 and over

observations.period: Summer 2026; everyday pressures and mental-health climate

denominator.unit: over 1,000 Irish adults aged 18 and over in a nationally representative survey

societal_anxiety.unit: percent believing there is a worrying amount of anxiety in society

mental_health_satisfaction.unit: percent reporting satisfaction with their own mental health

loneliness_isolation.unit: percent identifying loneliness and isolation as negatively influencing daily mental health and wellbeing

housing_concern.unit: percent naming housing concerns as negatively influencing mental health and wellbeing

climate_concern.unit: percent naming climate change as negatively influencing mental health and wellbeing

observations.method: Coyne Research survey commissioned by St Patrick's Mental Health Services, conducted over summer 2026 with a nationally representative sample of more than 1,000 adults.
observations.uncertainty: The public release reports perceived influences and satisfaction, not clinical diagnosis, symptom severity, exposure timing, household income, housing tenure, or causal effects.
observations.subgroup: Irish adults aged 18 and over; subgroup breakdowns are not fully reported on the release page.
observations.counterinterpretation: High societal anxiety and reported pressures may reflect heightened awareness or broad social interpretation rather than a direct measure of worsening clinical prevalence.

denominator.unit: over 1,000 Irish adults aged 18 and over in the survey; item-level bases are not separately disclosed

suicidal_thoughts_silence.unit: percent saying they would tell no one if experiencing suicidal thoughts

self_help_weakness.unit: percent considering it a sign of weakness if they sought help for a mental-health difficulty

friend_help_weakness.unit: percent considering it a sign of weakness if a friend sought help

support_gap.value: People may endorse mental-health openness in the abstract while retaining a sharper stigma around their own help-seeking and crisis disclosure.
support_gap.unit: analytical synthesis from published survey items

observations.method: Cross-sectional public-attitudes survey; the release reports item percentages but not item wording, response options, weighting details, or the full questionnaire.
observations.uncertainty: Stated intentions about disclosure are not observed disclosure behavior, crisis-service use, or treatment access. Percentages may use item-specific bases not disclosed in the release.
observations.subgroup: Irish adults; no public item-level subgroup profile on the release page.
observations.counterinterpretation: A willingness to tell no one may signal privacy, uncertainty about whom to trust, or question interpretation as well as stigma.

observations.period: Summer 2026; digital exposure and perceived mental-health risk

denominator.unit: over 1,000 Irish adults aged 18 and over in the survey; item-level bases are not separately disclosed

children_social_media_concern.unit: percent believing social-media and/or smartphone use is associated with mental-health difficulties in children

adult_social_media_concern.unit: percent believing social-media and/or smartphone use is associated with mental-health difficulties in adults

digital_risk_frame.value: Digital-media exposure is treated by a large majority as a mental-health risk across both children and adults.

observations.method: Descriptive attitudinal estimates from the St Patrick's Mental Health Services annual survey.
observations.uncertainty: Belief in an association does not establish device use, platform design, content exposure, dose, direction, or mental-health causality.
observations.subgroup: Irish adults; the release does not provide the age-specific bases or whether respondents answered for themselves, children, or society generally.
observations.counterinterpretation: Digital-media concern may be a proxy for wider worries about parenting, social change, youth wellbeing, or visibility of distress.

observations.period: 2020-2026 comparison; movement from distress to support-seeking

denominator.unit: 2026 survey respondents; historical comparison is reported by the publisher and item bases are not separately disclosed

experienced_difficulty_support.unit: percent of respondents who had experienced a mental-health difficulty and had sought support in 2026

discrimination_exposure.unit: percent saying they had been, or knew someone who had been, discriminated against due to mental-health difficulties

stigma_progress_belief.unit: percent believing people with mental-health difficulties experience less stigma and discrimination than 10 years ago

observations.method: Publisher-reported annual barometer comparison; the release does not provide the full historical questionnaire, harmonization protocol, or item-level denominators.
observations.uncertainty: The 2020 and 2026 estimates may differ in sample composition, wording, context, and reporting behavior; increased support-seeking is not proof of improved access or outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Respondents who report having experienced a mental-health difficulty, plus the full adult sample for discrimination and stigma-attitude items.
observations.counterinterpretation: Greater support-seeking may reflect both reduced stigma and greater perceived need; discrimination can remain common even while respondents perceive long-term improvement.

related_sources.claim: St Patrick's Mental Health Services publishes the 2026 survey findings, sample description, Coyne Research fieldwork attribution, and the reported attitudes and pressures.

boundary: This record identifies a public-attitudes and social-pressure mechanism linking material insecurity, loneliness, housing, climate concern, digital exposure, stigma, and help-seeking. It does not establish clinical prevalence, causal effects, service capacity, treatment quality, or individual risk prediction.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official St Patrick's Mental Health Services page was reviewed for its 2026 sample description, Coyne Research attribution, pressure, stigma, digital-media, discrimination, and support-seeking findings.
